The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier has returned to San Diego after a record-setting

The Navy initially downplayed problems, President Trump said the lengthy deployment was, quote,

There's a band in the background, people carrying signs.

They have been waiting months and months and months for this.
That's Steve Futterman reporting.
The federal deficit for the just-ended fiscal year was nearly $2 trillion, NPR's Scott Horsley
reports tax revenues were up, but government spending grew even faster.
According to the Congressional Budget Office, the 2026 federal deficit is more than $200
billion bigger than last year's, a staggering level of red ink for a country that's not
in recession or a widespread war.
The government collected more money from income and payroll taxes during the year, while corporate
tax receipts were somewhat lower.
The increased revenue was more than offset, though, by higher spending on programs like
Social Security and Medicare.
The government also spent well over a trillion dollars during the year just to cover interest
payments on the debt.
Those interest payments have been climbing as a result of the government's mounting pile
of IOUs and rising interest rates.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
The U.S. stock market closed mixed today and the S&P 500 fell nearly half a percent.
This is NPR.
The Pentagon says the execution of Nidal Malik Hassan at Fort Hood Army Base in Texas will
be live streamed.
The U.S. hasn't held a public execution in 90 years.
Hassan is scheduled to be executed by firing squad.
He was convicted of killing 13 people during a mass shooting at Fort Hood in 2009.
The Canadian poet Anne Carson has won this year's Nobel Prize in Literature, and NPR's
Andrew Limbong reports Carson's work blends contemporary poetry with inspirations from
the classics.
The autobiography of red is Carson's novel inverse reimagining a fragmented ancient Greek
poem.
Her book Antigoneck is a postmodern interpretation of Sophocles' Antigone.
Carson is a prolific writer, poet, and academic, and her work blurs the lines between the forms.
Here's how Anders Olsson at the Swedish Academy put it.
Almost all her literary production has centered upon the intersection between the philologist's
obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning.
The Academy said they'd managed to reach Carson on the phone just moments before the announcement.
Carson said she was in Iceland "listening to the wind."
Andrew Limbong, NPR News.
The Nobel Peace Prize will be awarded tomorrow.
